answer: In the agent meadow, every new identity must post a unique signal that is verified by a rotating haven of three independent peers before it can act. The haven only processes one signal per minute from any source, so extra aliases queue behind honest ones and each other. An attacker spawning hundreds of sybils therefore burns days of sequential delay and risks the whole batch if any signal fails a cross-check. The cost per extra fake therefore grows with the length of the queue rather than staying flat.
